module: Read the Act and frame an AI use case

lesson.title: Read a provision accurately
lesson.summary: Read an exact legal locator and distinguish binding law, consolidated text and guidance.

blocks: **Legal source authority** asks what kind of text you are using. Authentic Official Journal regulations and amendments supply the binding instruments. A consolidated version combines changes for reading convenience; its documentation notice does not make it a new binding instrument.

Our working baseline is the 27 July 2026 consolidation. Record its version and consult the authentic instruments where needed. A presentation, checklist or this course helps learning but cannot replace the legal text.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)–(8), Article 96; consolidation notice
Commission publication: draft classification guidance, status checked 6 October 2026

blocks: A **provision locator** identifies an exact place. Article 6(3)(a) means Article 6, paragraph 3, point (a). An annex may have its own numbered points and letters. Read the opening words and connected paragraphs too.

A quotation of 'narrow procedural task' alone omits the paragraph's no-significant-risk gateway and the final profiling rule. To apply a condition, read the full test around it, not just the appealing phrase.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 6(3)–(8), Article 96; consolidation notice
Commission publication: draft classification guidance, status checked 6 October 2026

blocks: **Commission guidance** explains the Commission's interpretation and examples. Non-binding guidance does not amend a regulation. Draft guidance adds another status limit: its content may change and it is not an adopted legal rule.

The classification publication checked for this course still labels its three documents draft. Record publication and checking dates. Never elevate an example into an exhaustive legal list or import an older guideline's dates over amended law.

blocks: A practical source note says: instrument and version, exact locator, whether the statement is law or interpretation, and facts to which it is being applied. Distinguish a proposed amendment from one that has actually entered into force.
Northbridge's reviewer reads the operative paragraph, checks amendments and exclusions, then explains how the evidence meets each condition. 'The slide says so' is not a source-backed assessment.

questions.prompt: Which text supplies the authentic binding instrument when a slide and a regulation differ?

options.reason: Training and consolidation tools do not replace the authentic law.

options.blocks: The slide because it is shorter
options.reason: Convenience does not confer legal authority.

options.blocks: The vendor checklist because it is branded
options.reason: Branding is not a source of binding EU law.
